Telecommunications · Nigerian complaint guidance

Telecom complaints about airtime, data, subscriptions and network service

Document airtime deductions, failed data bundles, unwanted subscriptions and unresolved telecom service problems before approaching the correct Nigerian provider or regulator.

By PetitionDesk Editorial Team · Reviewed 25 August 2026

Who this guide is for: Mobile and internet subscribers dealing with unexplained charges, poor connectivity, subscription problems or unresolved account restrictions.

Understand the problem before writing

A telecommunications complaint should identify the network operator, the affected service and the particular transaction or service interruption. Lost airtime, an unwanted recurring subscription, a failed data bundle and prolonged coverage problems involve different records and may need different internal teams.

Start by recording the affected phone number in a privacy-conscious format, the date and amount charged, any recharge or transaction reference and the service you expected to receive. Where an unwanted subscription is involved, state when you noticed it, whether you attempted to unsubscribe and what the operator or content provider communicated.

Network quality complaints should describe the location, dates, type of interruption and steps already taken. An isolated temporary outage is not the same as a repeated service failure affecting an area over several weeks. Screenshots, support chats and reference numbers help establish the pattern without relying on exaggerated claims.

Provider-first routing is especially important because the network operator controls account history, billing records and technical fault information. A regulator-stage complaint becomes stronger when it includes the operator's ticket number and a clear explanation of why the response was inadequate.

Build an evidence checklist

Use records that relate directly to your complaint. Put events in date order, identify the organisation involved, and keep copies of every message or acknowledgement. Describe what your documents actually show; do not present an allegation as a proven finding.

  • Network operator or internet-service provider
  • Affected line or account with unnecessary digits masked
  • Airtime, data or subscription amount and date
  • Support ticket, recharge reference or transaction receipt
  • Location and duration of any network problem
  • Screenshots and copies of prior operator communications

Choose the institution that can respond

Submit the initial complaint through the operator's official support, customer-care, app or complaint channel and request a ticket reference. Explain whether the desired result is a refund, cancellation, service restoration, billing explanation or correction of account records.

A company mentioned in a statement, address, receipt or background document is not automatically the institution responsible for the complaint. Identify who provided the disputed service, who made the decision, and who can supply records or correct the problem.

Decide whether escalation is justified

If the operator does not resolve the issue, provide the earlier ticket reference, complaint date, account details and response when using the Nigerian Communications Commission's published consumer-complaint process. Do not assume a regulator can investigate a matter that has no identifiable provider or support history.

Before escalating, keep the original complaint reference, the institution's written answer where available, and a concise explanation of what remains unresolved. Check the current instructions published by the relevant authority instead of assuming that one deadline applies to every type of complaint.

Worked example: applying the route in practice

If a data bundle was debited but never delivered, state the purchase date, bundle price, payment reference, account balance before and after, the operator's complaint reference and your request for delivery or refund.

Avoid common mistakes and protect personal data

Avoid sharing SIM-registration documents, full identity numbers, account passwords, one-time codes or unrelated private conversations when a masked transaction screenshot would be sufficient.

Remove passwords, one-time passcodes, card security codes and unrelated medical, financial or family information. Request a specific remedy supported by your evidence, such as an explanation, correction, investigation, refund or written decision.

Frequently asked questions

Should I keep the network provider's complaint ticket?

Yes. A support ticket or complaint reference helps the operator locate your case and supports a later regulator complaint if the issue remains unresolved.

Can I complain about an unwanted subscription?

Yes. Identify the date, amount, subscription label, relevant messages and any attempt to cancel so the operator can trace the billing event.

These links point to the organisations' published websites or complaint resources. Check that the channel and procedure remain current before sharing your complaint or evidence.
